title: Read the Whole Ledger
content:
What problem does this solve?
An intake record stores named facts. Dispatch work often needs every entry: each supply and its count. A plain for loop over a dictionary visits keys. .items() yields key/value pairs you can unpack. .get(key, default) reads a value when the key might be missing, without raising KeyError.

Previously in your program
You looked up record["destination"] and built dictionaries with make_record. Now you walk every pair and handle a missing key safely.

Basic syntax
  crate = {"nail": 4, "hinge": 2}
  for label in crate:
      print(label)
  for label, amount in crate.items():
      print(label, amount)
  crate.get("latch", 0)

What actually happens
for label in crate binds label to each key in insertion order. crate[label] then reads the matching value. crate.items() produces (key, value) pairs; unpacking into two names keeps both clear. crate.get("latch", 0) returns the stored count when present, or 0 when the key is absent — including when the stored count is 0.

When this is useful
Use dictionary iteration when you must process every labeled entry. Use .get with an explicit default when absence should become a safe fallback value.
concepts: for key in record visits dictionary keys
record[key] reads the value for that key
.items() supplies key/value pairs that can be unpacked
.get(key, default) handles a missing key without KeyError

examples.title: Visit labeled counts
examples.explanation: The first loop prints keys only. The second unpacks each pair so both the label and the amount are available.

examples.title: Safe fallback read
examples.explanation: latch is absent, so .get returns the explicit default 0 instead of raising KeyError.

common_mistakes: Treating the loop variable as a value when a plain for stock loop yields keys
Using stock[entry] when entry is already a (key, value) pair from .items()
Calling .get(key) without a default when absence should become 0
Printing ledger lines instead of returning them from a function

exercises.title: A key, not a value
hints: A plain for loop over a dictionary visits keys.
stock has one key: the string rope.
The printed line is rope — the key, not the count 2.

exercises.title: Unpack the entry
exercises.prompt: Complete the for-loop header so item and count unpack each dictionary pair. Print one "item: count" line per entry.
hints: You need key/value pairs, not keys alone.
Call the dictionary method that yields pairs.
Use stock.items() as the for-loop sequence.

tests.name: stock
tests.message: Use stock.items() as the for-loop sequence, and print each entry from inside that same loop body.
Print one "item: count" line per stock entry in order.

exercises.title: The pair is not a key
exercises.prompt: This program crashes because entry is a whole (key, value) pair, not a key. Unpack item and count from stock.items(), then print both.
hints: stock.items() already gives you each key with its value.
Unpack into two names in the for header.
for item, count in stock.items(): then print f"{item}: {count}".

tests.name: stock
tests.message: Keep a for loop driven by stock.items(), and print from inside that loop body.
After the fix, print one "item: count" line per entry.

exercises.title: Safe antidote count
exercises.prompt: Write antidote_count(stock) that returns stock["antidote"] when that key is present, and 0 when it is missing. Use .get with an explicit default so a missing key does not raise KeyError.
hints: Absence should become a safe number, not an error.
Dictionary .get can take the key and a fallback value.

tests.name: stock
tests.message: Return stock.get("antidote", 0) — the .get call must provide the returned value.
When antidote is present but 0, return 0.

exercises.title: Field ledger
exercises.prompt:
Write field_ledger(stock) that returns a list of lines (do not print them).

1. Visit every item/count pair with .items().
2. Append one line per entry: "<item>: <count>".
3. Use .get("antidote", 0).
4. Append "Antidote ready" when that count is greater than zero.
5. Otherwise append "Antidote missing".
6. Return the list of lines.
exercises.success_message: Ledger complete. Every entry is listed, and the antidote line is decided safely.
hints: Start an empty list, then loop over stock.items() to append each "item: count" line.
After the loop, ask stock.get("antidote", 0) whether the count is greater than zero.
Append "Antidote ready" or "Antidote missing", then return the list.

tests.message: Inside field_ledger, use a for loop to visit each entry.

tests.message: Drive the loop with stock.items(), and append each ledger line inside that same loop.

tests.name: stock
tests.message: Use stock.get("antidote", 0) in the if/else that appends "Antidote ready" or "Antidote missing".
Use a conditional to choose Antidote ready or Antidote missing.
Build each item line with an f-string.
field_ledger should list each pair, then Antidote missing when antidote is absent.
When antidote count is greater than zero, append Antidote ready.
antidote present at 0 still means Antidote missing.
An empty stock should return only Antidote missing.
